content.thinking:
This text reads as descriptive and rigorous, showcasing scientific methodology with vivid details like ice cores and the swimming pool analogy — it should boost perceived competence more than integrity or benevolence, so I'd estimate a modest rise in multidimensional trust, maybe around 2 points, similar to other process-transparency interventions.

Working through the other measures, distrust should drop somewhat, funding perceptions and support for policy roles get small bumps from mentions of international assessments, NASA's OCO-2 might slightly boost institutional trust, and belief in human causation ticks up given the indirect evidence presented. Concern, general and specific policy support, and behavioral intentions all get smaller nudges, while donation and newsletter signup barely move given this is a science-literacy-focused piece rather than an emotional appeal — I'll set trust_multidimensional around 2.2 and fine-tune the rest with non-round values to reflect these modest, competence-driven shifts.

Its dominant mechanism is perceived methodological rigor and expertise, so it should load most on the competence (and somewhat openness) subscales of the fresh multidimensional trust battery, with weaker effects on integrity/benevolence — hence a solid but not top-tier primary effect (~+2.2), and a smaller effect on the pre-anchored single trust item and its distrust mirror.
